about: Blind evaluation corpus for Precedent, written without looking at the parser or matcher. 92 decisions across nine domains, worded the way engineers, PMs, designers, security and compliance people actually record them in Confluence decision items, ADR pages and Jira 'Decision:' comments, plus work items worded like real Jira tickets. Decision annotation: chosen and rejected hold minimal noun phrases taken from the statement (leading verbs, articles, rationale, deadlines and the scope clause removed; meaningful modifiers kept; lists split). Options that were compared but not picked count as rejected. scope says where the decision applies and is [] when none is stated; deadlines and date windows are never scope. A rule with no named option puts the required thing in chosen and what it governs in scope. For action prohibitions ('never log X', 'do not store X in Y', 'don't send X to Y') rejected holds the object X and scope holds the place, channel or destination Y when one is named; the verb itself is not part of any field. Work labels are from the decision's point of view: conflict = the work adopts something the decision ruled out within its scope, undoes or replaces what it chose, or breaks its rule; aligned = the work implements or follows it, including removing or migrating off the ruled-out thing and tests that enforce it; related = same topic but neither follows nor contradicts it (investigations, spikes, docs, tuning, maintenance, or a use outside the decision's scope that is still worth seeing); none = no meaningful relation, including the same word used in another sense. Unlisted pairs are none; explicit none entries mark deliberate hard negatives. An array label means both readings are defensible, preferred one first, and the note explains why. D13 supersedes D12 (ADR-007); because D12 is no longer in force, pairs with D12 are labelled at most related. Review pass (after the blind draft): eight labels were adjusted for consistency (each note says why), ten reviewer work items (origin "reviewer") add cloud product names and abbreviations, and parseChecks holds parse-only statements from live UI tests and a known-gap list; they are not indexed because several would contradict decisions above. Everything else has origin "blind". Two later groups are reported separately: origin "lead-blind" holds the cases the project lead reported from their own blind test, and origin "held-out" is a small set in a different voice (terse titles, business rules, non-native phrasing) written before the matcher was tuned further and never tuned against. Origin "lead-blind-2" holds the lead's second blind set (reported cases, reconstructed from their notes). Origin "lead-blind-3" holds the lead's third blind set (ten decisions as typed and the work items reported with them; four aligned items were reported without their wording and are reconstructed, each marked in its note). It was written against the phrase-pattern matcher and is the set the matcher was restructured around, so it is in-sample for everything after it. Origin "lead-blind-4" holds the lead's fourth blind set, run against the adoption-evidence matcher: the decisions and work items the lead reported, with three decisions and four aligned items reconstructed where only their verdicts were reported (each marked in its note). Everything after it is in-sample for this set too. Origin "agent-held-out" is a small group in another voice (marketing ops, legal, IT and mobile notes; terse and lower-case in places) written by the engineer of the adoption-evidence matcher after the restructuring and before the default-adoption rule, without running any of it. It was measured once before that rule and once after, and nothing was tuned on it between the two measurements; anything committed later may have been informed by it. Origin "agent-held-out-2" is a second group by the same engineer, written after the fixes the first one prompted and run once: customer success, finance, data, security, IT and hiring notes, mostly naming tools no lexicon knows. It is recorded as it was measured; what was changed afterwards is said in the commit that changed it. Origin "lead-blind-5" holds the lead's fifth blind set: ten plain tech-choice decisions and 27 work items, worded the way a judge is most likely to type them, as reported.
